Maya: Heads-up — I opened a docs PR to backfill SDK streaming examples to the new cursor API + retry semantics. PR #4523. Need a quick sanity pass for Python/TypeScript/Go samples and to fix a couple broken links to the pagination guide.

Dan: Thanks — pinged the PR: https://git.redwood/infra/docs/pull/4523. I can take Go + TS samples today. One question: do we want to document `stop_on_eof` behavior vs cursor end explicitly?

Sahil: Quick runtime note: we changed partial-stream error handling — backpressure now triggers a resume retry using an idempotency token. I can add a short blurb + example of how clients should resume.

Elena: I'll run the examples locally. Maya, can you add which model you validated with? small vs xlarge differ because of kv cache behavior.

Maya: Used redwood/conv-v1 with long-context flag. Repro steps are in the PR. Also found two broken links in the docs: /guides/pagination (404) and /sdk/python/streaming (404).

docs-bot: CI: docs build failed on link-check. Error: /sdk/python/streaming -> 404. See logs: https://ci.redwood/logs/4523 :warning:

Dan: I'll fix the doc pages and push a follow-up. For the Go sample I replaced the old `Stream()` loop with `StreamCursor()` and pushed commit a1b2c.

Sahil: Dropping the recommended retry policy for clients here. Suggested pseudo snippet for Python clients:

```py
# pseudo-client resume pattern
with client.stream(..., cursor=True) as s:
    for chunk in s:
        try:
            process(chunk)
        except TransientError:
            s.retry_with_token(token_id)
```

Use an idempotency token on resume to avoid double-effects.

Elena: Local runs are green for TS + Py after Dan's commit. One minor nit: TS example was using `await stream.next()` which can race during backoff; I changed it to `for await (const part of stream)` and it behaved more deterministically.

Maya: Great — I'll squash + rebase and add a short migration note that explains cursor vs old streaming behavior, links to the runtime retry policy, and fixes the two broken links.

Dan: LGTM. If someone can do a final wording/style review (docs tone + code style) that'd be great. Otherwise I'll merge tomorrow morning.

Sahil: I'll do a quick technical review now (~30m). If CI is green I'd prefer a canary merge.

docs-bot: CI: link-check passed; build: success. docs-publish scheduled. :tada:

Maya: Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with a changelog entry and a tiny example app in the examples repo to show resume+retry patterns.
